name: combine_mums
summary: MUMmer combineMUMs: extends the clusters of mgaps and aligns the gaps between their matches (edit distance), byte for byte.
short: MUMmer combineMUMs: extension and alignment of the mgaps clusters (-D -e -n -N -q -r -S -t -v -x -W), byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 combineMUMs: takes the clusters of exact matches of mgaps and extends every cluster off both ends and fills the gaps between its matches by edit-distance alignments (branch point score 0.272 per match in single precision, or 1 - (1 - errorRate) with -e; give up 200 bases past the best score, at most 500 errors, extensions in steps of 10 000 bases). Output: the gaps file with, under every gap line, the number of errors and the alignment of the gap with 10 bases of each flanking match, and a 'Region:' line after every combined region; -D writes only the positions of the differences, -S every difference, -v every extension, -n lets only a, c, g, t match, -N breaks matches at consecutive non-ACGT characters, -t tags with the FASTA headers, -x suppresses the cover files, -W names the errors file. Byte for byte equal to the installed combineMUMs on 240 + runs (every option, both strands, N / IUPAC characters, extensions of 24 kb) and 3 000 more random runs.

text: What combineMUMs writes to standard output.
errorsFile: The file -W names (witherrors.gaps): the gap lines with the number of errors appended.
messages: What the program writes to standard error: the summary of the matches and, without -x, the coverage of both sequences.
files: The files the program leaves behind by name: the errors file and the .cover files.

name: repeat_match
summary: MUMmer repeat-match: the maximal exact repeats of a sequence on both strands, in the order of the program's suffix tree, byte for byte.
short: MUMmer repeat-match: maximal exact repeats (-n -f -t -E -V) in the order of the program's suffix tree, byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 repeat-match (Delcher): the maximal exact repeats of the first sequence of a FASTA file that are at least minLength long (-n, default 20), within the forward strand and, unless forwardOnly (-f), between the forward and the reverse-complement strand. Output: 'Long Exact Matches:' and a line per match 'start1 start2[r] length' (start2 is a position of the reverse-complement strand, as a position of the original sequence read backwards, when the line has the letter r). tandemOnly (-t, implies forwardOnly) lists only the repeats whose two copies touch (start1 + length >= start2). The matches are listed in the order of the program's own suffix tree (a suffix tree of the sequence and of its reverse complement in which a new child is put in front of its siblings), reproduced by the same construction. exhaustive (-E) uses the program's quadratic search instead (a different order); verbose (-V 1) prints the sizes of the program's structures, -V 2 the construction and the traversal of the tree. messages = standard error ('Genome Length = n   Used m internal nodes', the warnings of the FASTA reader). A genome that is an exact reverse-complement palindrome stops the program (exitCode 255, '*** Genome is exact palindrome ***' on standard output). An empty file, a file without a '>' line (the program works on an uninitialised buffer: valgrind use of uninitialised values; the output changes under MALLOC_PERTURB_) and a header whose first word has 500 or more characters (buffer overflow, abort) are refused with an error. Byte for byte equal to the installed repeat-match on 370 + runs and 3 300 more random runs (every option, both strands, N / IUPAC characters, genomes of 30 kb).

name: exact_tandems
summary: MUMmer exact-tandems: the exact tandem repeats of a sequence (repeat-match -t | sort | tandem-repeat.awk) and the script as installed.
short: MUMmer exact-tandems: exact tandem repeats (repeat-match -t | sort | awk), the intended pipeline and the script as installed.
description: MUMmer 3.23 exact-tandems: the exact tandem repeats of the first sequence of a FASTA file with a duplicated unit of at least minLength bases. The script runs repeat-match -t -n N, drops its two header lines, sorts the matches by the first and second column (sort -k1n -k2n) and feeds them to tandem-repeat.awk, which writes the table 'Start Extent UnitLen Copies' with one line per repeat region (the first match of every start whose copies touch; extent = start2 + length - start1, unit = start2 - start1, copies = extent / unit with one decimal). By default (installedScript = false) the result is that intended pipeline. The script as installed by the Debian package is broken - its last command is split over two lines (awk -f $ and, on the next line, $scriptdir/tandem-repeat.awk) - so awk looks for a file named $ and fails with status 2 ('awk: fatal: cannot open source file `$' for reading: No such file or directory'); sh -e then stops the script without a table and without removing its temporary file: installedScript = true reproduces that (text = the two progress lines 'Finding matches' and 'Tandem repeats', exitCode 2, filesLeft = $$.tmp.matches). messages = standard error (the lines of repeat-match, then the awk error with installedScript). A minLength below 1 makes repeat-match fail (the table is just the header). Byte for byte equal to the installed script (installedScript = true) and to the pipeline run by hand on 215 + runs each and 1 200 more random runs each.

text: The table of tandem repeats (or the two progress lines of the installed script).
messages: The standard error of the script.
exitCode: The exit status (0; 2 for the installed script).
filesLeft: The files the script leaves behind ($$.tmp.matches for the installed script).

name: mapview
summary: MUMmer mapview: FIG maps of show-coords -rl alignments (percent identity along the reference, links between contig matches, genes), byte for byte.
short: MUMmer mapview: FIG maps of show-coords -rl / mgaps alignments with genes (-d -f -m -n -p -v -x1 -x2 -g -I -Ir), byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 mapview (perl script): FIG 3.2 files of the alignments of a show-coords -rl file (or mgaps output) along the reference, with the genes of a UTR and a CDS GFF file; -f pdf / ps through fig2dev (the command lines and the FIG texts are returned). example.title: A PNG plot of one alignment
example.prompt: Write the gnuplot script that plots this delta file as a PNG.

files.demo.gp:
set terminal png tiny size 800,800
set output "demo.png"
set size 1,1
set grid
unset key
set border 15
set tics scale 0
set xlabel "ref"
set ylabel "qry"
set format "%.0f"
set mouse format "%.0f"
set mouse mouseformat "[%.0f, %.0f]"
set xrange [1:260]
set yrange [1:240]
set style line 1  lt 1 lw 3 pt 6 ps 1
set style line 2  lt 3 lw 3 pt 6 ps 1
set style line 3  lt 2 lw 3 pt 6 ps 1
plot \
 "demo.fplot" title "FWD" w lp ls 1, \
 "demo.rplot" title "REV" w lp ls 2

output.messages:
Reading delta file x.delta
Writing plot files demo.fplot, demo.rplot
Writing gnuplot script demo.gp
Rendering plot demo.png

example.note: mummerplot -p demo --png x.delta: one forward alignment at 98.755 percent similarity; the axes are the reference and query lengths.
